chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies and there is no one with him to wash him except women. Can the women wash him? He said: His wife or the one with his sanctity (mahram) should wash him, and the women pour water over him by pouring from above the clothes.
ai.seo_question: How is a man washed by women if no men are available?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of janazah washing by distinguishing between the primary washer (the wife or mahram) and the assistants who pour water over the garments to preserve modesty (haya). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on gender-specific roles in ritual purity, ensuring that the body remains covered during the washing process to maintain dignity. The ruling underscores the practical application of mahram relationships in funerary rites when opposite-gender washing is restricted.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who is dying and there is no one in his presence who can wash him except for the women. Can the women wash him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His wife should wash him, or the one with sanctity (one he cannot be married to), and the (other) women would pour water with a pouring from above the clothes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-kindiy from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who dies and there is no one to give him Ghusl (bath) except women.
He (the Imam) said, ‘His wife can give him Ghusl (bath) or a woman of his relatives and other woman can just pour water from behind the cloth.’”
